result.title: Where slide-level foundation-model classifiers fail on atypical breast lesions
result.summary: Whether a ductal breast lesion is called atypical hyperplasia or low-grade carcinoma in situ increasingly determines surgery. However, slide-level classifiers built on pathology foundation models (PFMs) perform worst on these lesions. Using four PFMs, cross-validation on BRACS and preregistered hypotheses, we studied where the classification of atypia fails. Because slides are labelled with their most severe lesion, only 39% of the slides with annotated atypical ductal hyperplasia (ADH) were labelled ADH. Attention ranked the lesion high but rarely first, and showing the model only the lesion helped little, whereas classifiers trained per decision with lesion-level labels improved all four atypical boundaries. ADH regions inserted into benign slides raised the probability of malignancy more than that of atypia. In a hospital with pathologist-labelled single-subtype slides and in HISTAI, benign slides were scored closer to lesions and triage specificity fell from 0.48-0.53 to 0.00-0.07 and 0.22.

AI.brief_summary: 使用四个病理基础模型在 BRACS 等数据上交叉验证，定位 slide 级分类器在非典型乳腺病变上失败的原因，比较 attention 定位、仅输入病灶区域与按决策用病灶级标签训练分类器的效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其中「注意力把病灶排得很高但几乎不排第一」「只给模型看病灶帮助有限」这类诊断，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据是否真被使用、以及弱/错配标签下的贡献分配提供探针式评价参照，需核查其结论能否迁移。
